# Intersection of Two Arrays II. compare: unordered 0 accepts any order, but
# each value must be repeated exactly as often as expected; the expected
# answers below list the values in increasing order.

@example 3 occurs three times in nums1 and twice in nums2, so it is listed twice; 8 is in both once; 1 and 5 are in only one array.
[3,1,3,3,8]
[3,8,3,5]
=> [3,3,8]

@example nums2 repeats 2 and 6, but nums1 has each only once.
[6,2]
[2,2,2,6,6]
=> [2,6]

@example No value occurs in both arrays.
[4,4]
[7]
=> []

# Single elements, equal.
[0]
[0]
=> [0]

# Single elements, different.
[1000]
[999]
=> []

# The bounds 0 and 1000, repeated.
[0,0,1000,1000,1000]
[1000,0,1000]
=> [0,1000,1000]

# Identical arrays give back the whole array.
[5,1,5,9]
[9,5,1,5]
=> [1,5,5,9]

# nums1 is contained in nums2, counting repeats.
[2,2,7]
[7,2,4,2,2]
=> [2,2,7]

# nums2 is contained in nums1, counting repeats.
[3,6,3,6,3]
[6,3]
=> [3,6]

# Many more copies in nums1 than in nums2.
[8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8]
[8,8]
=> [8,8]

# Disjoint arrays with repeats.
[1,1,2,2]
[3,3,4]
=> []

# The smaller count comes from nums1 for one value and from nums2 for another.
[5,5,5,6,7]
[7,7,6,6,6,5]
=> [5,6,7]

# Every value is shared, each with a different pair of counts.
[1,2,2,3,3,3]
[3,3,2,2,2,1,1]
=> [1,2,2,3,3]
